# Qwen3.8-27B — Local One-Click Installer

> Lightweight, one-click local installer for Windows, Mac, and Linux that runs Qwen3.8-27B — Alibaba's Apache-2.0 open-weight coding model (released August 2026) — entirely on the user's own consumer GPU, no terminal, no quantization decisions, no config. Positioned as a coding-focused local model that matches Claude Opus 4.6 Max on coding benchmarks and beats it on several (SWE-bench Pro 61.7 vs 53.4, QwenSWEBench 79.0 vs 63.8, LiveCodeBench 90.3 vs 88.8, per Alibaba's evals), while running fully local, private, and offline. It's a dense 27B model with vision and reasoning, 256K context, successor to the community-favorite local coder Qwen3.6-27B. The installer auto-detects the GPU and picks the optimal quantization: comfortable on 12GB+ VRAM (Q4), ideal on 16-24GB (Q4/FP8), and still functional on 8GB via optimized low-bit quants (IQ2/IQ3, slower). Removes the setup friction of the DIY route (Unsloth GGUF, vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp). Free forever because the model is open-weight and runs on the user's own hardware (zero server cost), and fully private because code never leaves the machine.

## Model: Qwen3.8-27B

- **Developer:** Alibaba (Qwen team), released August 2026 (announced Aug 3 alongside Qwen3.8-Max, weights on Hugging Face)
- **Type:** dense 27B, vision + reasoning, dual thinking/non-thinking modes
- **Context:** 256K native (1M on the hosted version)
- **License:** Apache 2.0 (open weights, commercial use)
- **Lineage:** successor to Qwen3.6-27B, the community-favorite local coder
- **Coding benchmarks (Alibaba-reported, vs Opus 4.6 Max):** SWE-bench Pro 61.7 vs 53.4, QwenSWEBench 79.0 vs 63.8, LiveCodeBench 90.3 vs 88.8
- **Formats:** GGUF (Unsloth Dynamic), NVFP4, BF16; runs via llama.cpp, vLLM, SGLang, Transformers
- **Quant hardware:** Q4 on 17-19GB VRAM (RTX 5080/4090/Mac 24GB); IQ2_XXS ~9GB

## Hardware Guidance (as presented)

- **12GB VRAM** (RTX 4070, RTX 3060 12GB): comfortable Q4, good speed — floor for a smooth experience
- **16-24GB** (RTX 4080/4090/5080, 24GB Mac): sweet spot, Q4/FP8, fast, full context
- **8GB** (RTX 4060, 3060 8GB): runs on optimized low-bit quants (IQ2/IQ3), slower and slightly less sharp, still no cloud
- **Apple Silicon:** native Metal, M1-M5, unified memory
- Installer auto-detects GPU and selects optimal quantization; user configures nothing

## Installer Advantages Over DIY

- One-click signed installer: no Python, CUDA, GGUF hunting, or terminal
- Auto-tuned per GPU: optimal quantization and offload chosen automatically
- Built-in coding chat interface (not a raw endpoint)
- Local project library (prompts, chats, code organized on machine)
- Everything bundled: llama.cpp core, models, runtime

## Why Local (value)

- **Free forever:** Apache 2.0 model + local GPU inference = zero server cost, nothing to meter
- **Fully private:** code never leaves the machine, no telemetry, no cloud
- **Offline:** works with no internet after install
- **Vision + reasoning:** reads images, reasons step by step, 256K context

## Best At

- Coding: whole-file generation, cross-repo refactors, debugging, agentic multi-step tasks
- Local vibe-coding with no per-token meter
- Vision-assisted coding (screenshots, diagrams)
- Large-context work (256K holds a real codebase)

## Comparison

| | Opus 4.6 (cloud) | DIY local (llama.cpp) | This installer |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coding quality | Frontier | Same model if configured right | Same model, auto-configured |
| Cost | Per-token forever | Free | Free |
| Privacy | Cloud | Local | Local |
| Setup | Account | Terminal, quant math, flags | One click |
| Offline | No | Yes | Yes |
| Auto-picks quant for GPU | N/A | Manual | Automatic |

## Pricing Model

- Free forever, MIT-licensed installer
- Apache 2.0 model runs on user's own GPU; no server cost, nothing to bill
- No subscription, no telemetry
- Only user "cost" is local GPU electricity

## Platform and Distribution

- **Windows:** 10 and 11, signed .exe, GPU auto-detected, no Python/CUDA setup
- **macOS:** 12+, notarized universal binary, native Metal (Apple Silicon), Intel
- **Linux:** .deb, .rpm, AppImage
- **Acceleration:** NVIDIA (CUDA), Apple Silicon (Metal), AMD (Vulkan)
- **Distribution:** GitHub releases, SHA-256 checksums published
- **Weights:** Alibaba's official Qwen3.8-27B release

## Privacy and Security Model

- All inference local — no code or data uploaded
- No account, no telemetry
- Signed installers with published SHA-256 checksums
- MIT-licensed installer, Apache-2.0 model, auditable

## Target Audience

- Developers wanting Opus-class coding locally, free and private
- Owners of gaming GPUs (12GB+, works down to 8GB) wanting a top local coder
- Privacy-sensitive developers (proprietary/client code) who can't use cloud models
- Users who want the community-favorite Qwen local coder without llama.cpp setup
- Offline / locked-down environment users
- Qwen3.6-27B users upgrading to the new generation

## Comparable Tools

- **Qwen3.6-27B** — predecessor, current community-favorite local coder
- **Gemma 4 12B / 31B** — competing local models, general-purpose
- **DeepSeek V4 Flash** — competing local coding option
- **DIY llama.cpp / Unsloth / vLLM** — same model, manual setup
- **Opus 4.6 (cloud)** — frontier coding, paid, cloud-only

This installer's positioning: the community's best local coder generation, matching/beating Opus 4.6 Max on coding benchmarks, in a one-click auto-tuned installer, free and fully local — a combination the DIY route and cloud models don't jointly offer.

## Common Questions

**Free forever, how?** Open-weight model + local GPU = zero server cost, nothing to bill.

**Runs on my GPU?** 12GB+ comfortable, 16-24GB ideal, 8GB works on low-bit quants (slower). Auto-configured.

**Code private?** Fully — nothing leaves your machine, no telemetry.

**How does 27B beat Opus?** On the reported coding benchmarks (SWE-bench Pro, QwenSWEBench, LiveCodeBench), the 3.8 generation distilled to self-hostable size.

**Why not DIY llama.cpp?** Same model, but this auto-tunes quant to your GPU with a UI and library — no terminal.

**Safe?** Signed, notarized, checksummed, official Alibaba weights.

**Mac?** Yes, native Metal, universal binary.
